title: find-unit
summary: Finds which indexed unit declares a symbol, and adds that unit to a file's uses clause
intro: Read this when a symbol is undeclared and you need the unit to add to uses. find-unit --name X --in file looks the declaring unit up in the index and can add it to the file (--apply, with a backup unless --no-backup). Without --apply it is a dry run: it prints the uses-clause edit, exits 0 and writes nothing (--json prints the edit set and never writes). Exit 0 for a preview, an applied edit or a unit already in uses; 1 when no unit declares the symbol or no edit can be computed; 2 on missing arguments or no database.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint find-unit --name <Symbol> --in <file> [--json|--apply|--no-backup] --db <db> - add the declaring unit to uses
help: drag-lint find-unit --name <Symbol> --in <file> [--json|--apply|--no-backup] --db <db>  - add the declaring unit to uses

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Find Unit for Symbol (add to uses)...
steps: Needs an index; for an RTL/VCL symbol use the platform library DB
drag-lint > Uses & Dependencies > Find Unit for Symbol (add to uses)...
The declaring unit is named; Yes adds it to the active unit's uses clause, No previews a dry run

pitfalls: for an RTL/VCL/third-party X, point --db at the PLATFORM LIBRARY database (resolve-dbs --platform win64) -- a project DB holds only that project's units.
